bug_semantics: The historical-log GET and SSE routes were placed on AuthRouterGroup, which authenticated a JWT but did not require an administrative scope, while the WebSocket route was placed on the middleware-free WSRouterGroup and its handler merely called ParseToken. Consequently any registered non-admin with a valid JWT could read stored LogEntry records and continuously receive new records, including caller paths, errors, module names, raw lines, and structured fields.
flaw_origin: fcbe5084a4f095760ac691039ef1999ce50db333 introduced the system-log feature and, in the same commit, first registered all three disclosure paths without an admin authorization check: internal/router/dashboard.go:8-11 added GET /api/system/logs, GET /api/system/logs/stream, and WS /ws/system/logs; internal/handler/dashboard/dashboard.go:86-160 added data-returning/streaming handlers, with the WebSocket handler checking only whether ParseToken succeeded at lines 119-132.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object names author and committer as L1nSn0w <l1nsn0w@qq.com>; its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory: https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/security/advisories/GHSA-w8jj-cwmc-wgq2 identifies the three routes, internal/router/dashboard.go, internal/handler/dashboard/dashboard.go, internal/service/dashboard/dashboard.go, and the exposed LogEntry fields; it reports affected <=4.2.1 and patched 4.4.3. Source history: `git log -L 5,10:internal/router/dashboard.go v4.4.2` and `git log -S '"/system/logs"' --all -- internal/router/dashboard.go` trace the vulnerable route additions to https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/commit/fcbe5084a4f095760ac691039ef1999ce50db333. That BIC added the routes at internal/router/dashboard.go:8-11, the unscoped handlers at internal/handler/dashboard/dashboard.go:86-160, the log-returning/streaming service in internal/service/dashboard/dashboard.go, and the sensitive LogEntry representation in internal/util/log/log.go. Direct-parent tree verification with `git show 51690dd61a629f7a0f1728583c6de55282699e70:internal/router/dashboard.go` shows only /dashboard/metrics routes and no system-log route, so the attack path is absent in the immediate parent. `git cat-file commit fcbe5084a4f095760ac691039ef1999ce50db333` proves the single parent, human author/committer identity, complete message, and absence of AI trailers. Version checks: the BIC is an ancestor of v4.0.0 (peeled commit 93b935c5b64020c7475abb9df071fdf8663b9f84), so the flaw predates the first v4 release. Contrary to the advisory's <=4.2.1 metadata, v4.2.2 (peeled commit 47bafa98941b6b583ee906933f4cd13be3b42054) and v4.4.2 (peeled commit 7b7890cbe294659df39c36feb51fcfbe9ec9bdb2) still contain all three unscoped routes. Commit https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/commit/6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 is absent from v4.4.2 and present in v4.4.3 (peeled commit b934467d26b91c96dc7c937b6a4e47d8d01484eb); its diff adds RequireScopes(ScopeAdminSettings) to only the historical GET and SSE routes. It leaves WS /system/logs unscoped, and the v4.4.3 handler still accepts any JWT via ParseToken. All-history `git log -G 'WSSubscribeSystemLogs|ScopeAdminSettings'` finds no later complete WebSocket authorization fix; audited HEAD 5ce1dd0a3d7092be537fb309a8685d024e8986de still registers the naked WS route at internal/router/dashboard.go:23 and still only parses a token at internal/handler/dashboard/dashboard.go:111-123. Thus 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 is fix evidence for two transports, not a complete fix SHA for the advisory's three-transport mechanism. fix_sha corrected from None to null (no complete fix; 6df56730 is partial HTTP-only) (reconciliation 2026-08-29: show 6df56730 rewrites only the two HTTP GETs with middleware.RequireScopes(ScopeAdminSettings); the WS route line 'appRouterGroup.WSRouterGroup.GET("/system/logs", ...)' is untouched (present in diff context, unchanged). reasoning: Field reconciliation 2026-08-29 (see evidence tail). Field reconciliation 2026-08-29 (see evidence tail). The vulnerable resource did not exist before fcbe5084a4f095760ac691039ef1999ce50db333: its immediate parent lacks every system-log route, whereas the BIC atomically adds the sensitive log model/service, three externally reachable endpoints, and handlers that rely on authentication rather than administrative authorization. Later removal/refactor commits merely preserve or move those lines, so they are not smaller introducers; the BIC is a normal one-parent feature commit and requires no squash decomposition. Its placement before v4.0.0 matches the vulnerable release history, while direct tag-tree inspection proves the advisory's <=4.2.1 affected bound is too narrow because v4.2.2 through v4.4.2 remain vulnerable. The v4.4.3 boundary contains 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313, which closes the HTTP and SSE paths with admin:settings scope enforcement, but both v4.4.3 and current public history leave the WebSocket path authorized by token validity alone. The complete issue is therefore still unpatched and no commit can honestly be recorded as fix_sha/direct_fix_sha. AI attribution is nevertheless closed: only the BIC commit object governs the verdict, and that object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, yielding NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: UNPATCHED: no commit in the available complete public history adds an admin/scope/role authorization check to WS /ws/system/logs; v4.4.3's 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 patch fixes only GET /api/system/logs and GET /api/system/logs/stream, and audited HEAD 5ce1dd0a3d7092be537fb309a8685d024e8986de still accepts any valid JWT on the WebSocket endpoint. Therefore there is no complete 40-hex fix SHA to report.

unpatched.reason: No commit in the available complete public history adds admin/scope/role authorization to WS /ws/system/logs; the v4.4.3 patch 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 fixes only the GET and SSE transports, and audited HEAD 5ce1dd0a3d7092be537fb309a8685d024e8986de still registers the naked WS route at internal/router/dashboard.go:23.

potential_fix.approach: Register the WebSocket /ws/system/logs route behind the same authenticated admin middleware group as the fixed GET/SSE transports and reject connections lacking a valid admin token before upgrading.
potential_fix.rationale: Requiring an admin-authenticated upgrade closes the third transport left open by the existing patch, completing the advisory's three-transport mechanism remediation.
